identification.title: Echo Holy
identification.album: Things of Heaven (Where We Come From)
identification.notes: Written by Jake Espy, Kory Miller, Mia Fieldes and Ran Jackson; copyright 2021 Songs From Richmond Park, Be Essential Songs, Upside Down Under and Songs of Red Rocks Worship Publishing, administered by Essential Music Publishing; CCLI 7162703; original key B per PraiseCharts. The list's guess of Vertical Worship is wrong: Essential Music Publishing and PraiseCharts both credit Red Rocks Worship. Catalogues disagree on the copyright year (2020 on one PraiseCharts listing, 2021 on the publisher's page), so 2021 follows the publisher. Also issued as a studio single and in a live recording from Littleton, which the text was read from. Reviewed as the song, not as any one recording.

claims.structuralNotes: A verse, a short pre-chorus extended on its second pass, a chorus that is sung four times with echoes and a doubled final return, a second verse, a post-chorus of holy and worthy, a four-line bridge, a last chorus and a brief outro that names Jesus. The verses picture the heavenly scene in first person: the throne, angels falling down and crying holy. The pre-chorus, post-chorus and outro address God and Jesus directly. God is declared worthy of glory, honor, dominion, power, wisdom and wonder, and holy. The end of the song speaks of a throne of grace. The verses and chorus also report the singer's own response, the heart unable to keep from singing and breath taken by majesty. No act of God is named: no creation, incarnation, cross, resurrection or return. The Spirit is not named; Jesus is named once, in the outro.

claims.claim: God is holy, and heaven rings with that cry before his throne.
claims.subject: The holiness of God

claims.claim: Angels fall down before the throne and worship.
claims.subject: Heavenly worship

claims.claim: God is worthy of glory, honor, dominion, power, wisdom and wonder.
claims.subject: The worthiness of God

claims.claim: The singer's heart is moved to sing and the majesty of God takes the breath away.
claims.subject: The response of the worshipper

claims.claim: The throne is a throne of grace that the singer approaches.
claims.subject: Access to God

claims.claim: The song ends by naming Jesus.
claims.subject: The person of Christ

strengths.title: The holiness of God sung as heaven sings it
strengths.explanation: The song is built on the cry of holy before the throne. It puts the congregation in the scene of Isaiah's and John's visions and keeps the attention on who God is, not on the singer.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The seraphim crying holy before the throne - the scene the song takes up.

strengths.title: Worthiness grounded in who God is
strengths.explanation: God is called worthy of glory, honor, power, wisdom and wonder, which is Scripture's own list of what the Lamb receives. Worship is therefore answered to God's worth, not to the singer's mood.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Worthy is the Lamb to receive power, wisdom, honor and glory - the heavenly list the song echoes.

strengths.title: A throne of grace
strengths.explanation: The close speaks of a throne of grace, which tells the congregation that the holy God can be approached. It tempers the awe of the song with welcome.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Drawing near to the throne of grace with confidence - the picture the song ends on.

doctrinesAffirmed: The worthiness of God to receive all glory
theological.assessment: Nothing to correct. The song says that God is holy and worthy and that heaven worships him, and each claim is true and taken from Isaiah and Revelation. The line about the heavenly song being known to every heart is poetic rather than a claim of innate worship. What it lacks is any act of God: the cross, resurrection and the Spirit are not reached, and Jesus is named once.

strengths.title: An anthem the room can join
strengths.explanation: The chorus is short and returns often, and the post-chorus and bridge are brief. A congregation learns it on the first pass and can lift it together.

strengths.title: A call to worship or a response to a reading
strengths.explanation: The subject is God's holiness and the heavenly scene, which suits an opening or a response after a reading from Isaiah 6 or Revelation 4.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Published original key is B per PraiseCharts. No chart was read, so no pitches are stated; check the chorus against the room before choosing a key.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The chorus is sung four times with echoes and a doubled last return. What repeats is the cry of holy, which keeps focus on God, but the repetition carries the arrangement more than it adds content.
communal.assessment: Anthemic and learnable, with a chorus the room can take up. The echoes and builds belong to the recording and can pull a leader toward performance, so the arrangement is better kept simple for congregational use. The first-person verses report the singer's response alongside the heavenly scene.

strengths.title: The subject is never in doubt
strengths.explanation: From the first pass the song is plainly about God's holiness and worth. A visitor knows what is being sung and to whom.

clarity.assessment: Clear in what it says. It states no act of God and names Jesus only once, so it does not by itself tell the gospel. A congregation singing it would know God is holy and worthy but not why one may approach him.

synthesis.summary: An anthem on the holiness and worthiness of God, drawing on the throne scenes of Isaiah and Revelation, with a close on the throne of grace. God is named and the Scripture is faithfully used. No act of God is stated, the voice mixes confession with the singer's own response, and Jesus is named once at the end. Nothing in it is false. No independent assessment of its teaching was found.

scriptureReferences.relevance: Seraphim crying holy before the throne - the song's central scene.
The living creatures and elders worshipping before the throne.
Worthy is the Lamb to receive glory, honor and power.
Greatness, power, glory and majesty belong to the Lord.
Approach the throne of grace with confidence - the close of the song.
All heaven praising God - the vision behind the heavenly chorus.
